programme.title: Artsnight
programme.sub-title: The Brits Who Designed the Modern World
programme.desc: British designers have revolutionised our homes, our workplaces and our public institutions. Arts reporter Brenda Emmanus meets and profiles our `Top 10', to find out what inspires them to make such phenomenal objects.

programme.title: Ian Rankin Investigates: Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
programme.desc: Crime writer Ian Rankin investigates The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde. Starting with Robert Louis Stevenson's nightmare in September 1885, Rankin traces the roots of this story, which stretches back to Stevenson's childhood.

programme.title: City Beneath the Waves: Pavlopetri
programme.desc: Off the southern coast of mainland Greece lies the oldest submerged city in the world, Pavlopetri. Led by underwater archaeologist Dr Jon Henderson, an international team of experts attempt to prise age-old secrets from the complex of streets and stone buildings laying less than five metres below the surface. State-of-the-art CGI helps to raise the city from the seabed for the first time in 3500 years.

programme.title: Thailand: Earth's Tropical Paradise
programme.desc: Southern Thailand is the Thailand people think they know. It is a place of both spectacular natural beauty and of wild parties, but behind this well-known image is also a place of unexpected surprise, where spirituality pervades every bit of life. For the animals that live here, this is natural wonderland.

programme.title: Yorkshire Wolds Way
programme.desc: The trail starts at the Humber Estuary and ends at the Yorkshire seaside resort of Filey. On the way, Paul takes in the views of the Yorkshire Wolds from the top of the Humber Bridge, learns to ride a penny farthing and searches out the spots made internationally famous by the artist David Hockney.

programme.title: Pubs, Ponds, and Power: The Story of the Village
programme.desc: Archaeologist Ben Robinson explores Lavenham in Suffolk, the best-preserved medieval village in the country. In the 16th century Lavenham was one of the wealthiest places in England, becoming rich on its woollen cloth industry, but the industry declined and the wealthy abandoned Lavenham. By the 19th century it was a place of poverty, but today it is once more a jewel of a village.

programme.title: The Guns of Navarone
programme.desc: A small group of commandos, led by Captain Keith Mallory, are assigned to attack and destroy the eponymous guns - installed on the side of a mountain - that are preventing allied ships from rescuing 2,000 trapped British soldiers. Unable to attack by air or sea, the crack team is sent in but it seems there is a turncoat amongst them.

programme.title: The Eagle Has Landed
programme.desc: In a daring kidnap attempt, a small force of crack German paratroopers are poised to snatch Winston Churchill and return with him to Germany. If they succeed in their mission, it could alter the course of the war.
